requirements.quote:
If a pair of BGP speakers try to establish a BGP connection with each
   other simultaneously, then two parallel connections well be formed.
   If the source IP address used by one of these connections is the same
   as the destination IP address used by the other, and the destination
   IP address used by the first connection is the same as the source IP
   address used by the other, connection collision has occurred.  In the
   event of connection collision, one of the connections MUST be closed.
requirements.condition: Two parallel BGP connections have reciprocal source and destination IP addresses.
requirements.required_behavior: Recognize the pair as a connection collision.
requirements.why_checkable: The source and destination address comparison is an exact predicate.

requirements.quote:
If a pair of BGP speakers try to establish a BGP connection with each
   other simultaneously, then two parallel connections well be formed.
   If the source IP address used by one of these connections is the same
   as the destination IP address used by the other, and the destination
   IP address used by the first connection is the same as the source IP
   address used by the other, connection collision has occurred.  In the
   event of connection collision, one of the connections MUST be closed.
requirements.required_behavior: MUST close one of the colliding connections.
requirements.why_checkable: Collision detection state and connection selection can be checked against this rule.

requirements.quote:
Based on the value of the BGP Identifier, a convention is established
   for detecting which BGP connection is to be preserved when a
   collision occurs.  The convention is to compare the BGP Identifiers
   of the peers involved in the collision and to retain only the
   connection initiated by the BGP speaker with the higher-valued BGP
   Identifier.
requirements.condition: Selecting which connection to preserve when a connection collision occurs.
requirements.required_behavior: Compare the BGP Identifiers of the two peers.
requirements.why_checkable: Collision detection state and connection selection can be checked against this rule.

requirements.quote:
Based on the value of the BGP Identifier, a convention is established
   for detecting which BGP connection is to be preserved when a
   collision occurs.  The convention is to compare the BGP Identifiers
   of the peers involved in the collision and to retain only the
   connection initiated by the BGP speaker with the higher-valued BGP
   Identifier.
requirements.condition: A connection collision occurs between peers with different BGP Identifiers.
requirements.required_behavior: Retain only the connection initiated by the speaker with the higher BGP Identifier.
requirements.why_checkable: Collision detection state and connection selection can be checked against this rule.

requirements.quote:
Upon receipt of an OPEN message, the local system MUST examine all of
   its connections that are in the OpenConfirm state.  A BGP speaker MAY
   also examine connections in an OpenSent state if it knows the BGP
   Identifier of the peer by means outside of the protocol.  If, among
   these connections, there is a connection to a remote BGP speaker
requirements.condition: Upon receipt of an OPEN message.
requirements.required_behavior: MUST examine all local connections in OpenConfirm state for collisions.
requirements.why_checkable: The OPEN handler and its enumeration of OpenConfirm connections can be inspected.

requirements.quote:
Upon receipt of an OPEN message, the local system MUST examine all of
   its connections that are in the OpenConfirm state.  A BGP speaker MAY
   also examine connections in an OpenSent state if it knows the BGP
   Identifier of the peer by means outside of the protocol.  If, among
   these connections, there is a connection to a remote BGP speaker
requirements.condition: Upon receipt of an OPEN message, if the peer BGP Identifier is known by means outside the protocol.
requirements.required_behavior: MAY also examine connections in OpenSent state for collisions.
requirements.why_checkable: The optional OpenSent collision examination has a checkable prerequisite: external knowledge of the peer Identifier.

requirements.quote:
Upon receipt of an OPEN message, the local system MUST examine all of
   its connections that are in the OpenConfirm state.  A BGP speaker MAY
   also examine connections in an OpenSent state if it knows the BGP
   Identifier of the peer by means outside of the protocol.  If, among
   these connections, there is a connection to a remote BGP speaker

RFC 4271                         BGP-4                      January 2006

   whose BGP Identifier equals the one in the OPEN message, and this
   connection collides with the connection over which the OPEN message
   is received, then the local system performs the following collision
   resolution procedure:
requirements.condition: On receipt of OPEN, an examined connection has a remote BGP Identifier equal to that in the OPEN message and collides with the connection receiving OPEN.
requirements.required_behavior: Perform the specified collision resolution procedure.
requirements.why_checkable: Identifier equality and connection collision gate the resolution procedure.

requirements.quote:
1) The BGP Identifier of the local system is compared to the BGP
         Identifier of the remote system (as specified in the OPEN
         message).  Comparing BGP Identifiers is done by converting them
         to host byte order and treating them as 4-octet unsigned
         integers.
requirements.condition: Comparing local and remote BGP Identifiers in the collision resolution procedure.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the remote BGP Identifier specified in the received OPEN message.
requirements.why_checkable: The source of the remote Identifier operand can be inspected.

requirements.quote:
1) The BGP Identifier of the local system is compared to the BGP
         Identifier of the remote system (as specified in the OPEN
         message).  Comparing BGP Identifiers is done by converting them
         to host byte order and treating them as 4-octet unsigned
         integers.
requirements.condition: Comparing BGP Identifiers for collision resolution.
requirements.required_behavior: Convert the Identifiers to host byte order before comparing.
requirements.why_checkable: The byte-order conversion used by the comparison is checkable.

requirements.quote:
1) The BGP Identifier of the local system is compared to the BGP
         Identifier of the remote system (as specified in the OPEN
         message).  Comparing BGP Identifiers is done by converting them
         to host byte order and treating them as 4-octet unsigned
         integers.
requirements.condition: Comparing BGP Identifiers for collision resolution.
requirements.required_behavior: Treat the Identifiers as 4-octet unsigned integers.
requirements.why_checkable: The width and signedness of comparison operands can be inspected.

requirements.quote:
2) If the value of the local BGP Identifier is less than the
         remote one, the local system closes the BGP connection that
         already exists (the one that is already in the OpenConfirm
         state), and accepts the BGP connection initiated by the remote
         system.
requirements.condition: Collision resolution: the local BGP Identifier is less than the remote BGP Identifier.
requirements.required_behavior: Close the already existing BGP connection in OpenConfirm state.
requirements.why_checkable: Collision detection state and connection selection can be checked against this rule.

requirements.quote:
2) If the value of the local BGP Identifier is less than the
         remote one, the local system closes the BGP connection that
         already exists (the one that is already in the OpenConfirm
         state), and accepts the BGP connection initiated by the remote
         system.
requirements.condition: Collision resolution: the local BGP Identifier is less than the remote BGP Identifier.
requirements.required_behavior: Accept the connection initiated by the remote system.
requirements.why_checkable: Collision detection state and connection selection can be checked against this rule.

requirements.quote:
2) If the value of the local BGP Identifier is less than the
         remote one, the local system closes the BGP connection that
         already exists (the one that is already in the OpenConfirm
         state), and accepts the BGP connection initiated by the remote
         system.

      3) Otherwise, the local system closes the newly created BGP
         connection (the one associated with the newly received OPEN
         message), and continues to use the existing one (the one that
         is already in the OpenConfirm state).
requirements.condition: Collision resolution: the local BGP Identifier is greater than or equal to the remote BGP Identifier.
requirements.required_behavior: Close the newly created connection associated with the newly received OPEN message.
requirements.why_checkable: Collision detection state and connection selection can be checked against this rule.

requirements.quote:
2) If the value of the local BGP Identifier is less than the
         remote one, the local system closes the BGP connection that
         already exists (the one that is already in the OpenConfirm
         state), and accepts the BGP connection initiated by the remote
         system.

      3) Otherwise, the local system closes the newly created BGP
         connection (the one associated with the newly received OPEN

requirements.condition: Collision resolution: the local BGP Identifier is greater than or equal to the remote BGP Identifier.
requirements.required_behavior: Continue using the existing connection in OpenConfirm state.
requirements.why_checkable: Collision detection state and connection selection can be checked against this rule.

requirements.quote:
Unless allowed via configuration, a connection collision with an
   existing BGP connection that is in the Established state causes
   closing of the newly created connection.
requirements.condition: A connection collides with an existing connection in Established state, unless allowed via configuration.
requirements.why_checkable: Collision detection state and connection selection can be checked against this rule.

requirements.quote:
Note that a connection collision cannot be detected with connections
   that are in Idle, Connect, or Active states.
requirements.condition: Connections are in Idle, Connect, or Active state.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Detect a connection collision with these connections.
requirements.why_checkable: The eligible states for collision detection can be checked.

requirements.quote:
Closing the BGP connection (that results from the collision
   resolution procedure) is accomplished by sending the NOTIFICATION
   message with the Error Code Cease.
requirements.condition: Closing a BGP connection as a result of collision resolution.
requirements.required_behavior: Send a NOTIFICATION message with Error Code Cease.
requirements.error_behavior: Send a NOTIFICATION message with Error Code Cease.
requirements.why_checkable: The collision-close path emits a checkable message type and error code.
